test.title: Laws of Motion - Test 3
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: At any instant the velocity of a particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mo>+</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> . If the force acting on the particle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mo>+</mo><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> . Then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> will be:

For a free body diagram shown in the figure, the four forces are applied in the 'x' and 'y' directions. What additional force must be applied and at what angle with positive x-axis so that the net acceleration of body is zero?

Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The limiting force of static friction depends on the area of contact and independent of materials.
Statement (II) : The limiting force of kinetic friction is independent of the area of contact and depends on materials.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
